title: Plush dragon physics comparison
author: vib3coded
prompt:
Build "Plush Dragon" — Material Studies No. 014: a single self-contained HTML file, native WebGPU, fully procedural (no assets, no libraries), in the same editorial style as the series (serif masthead, side specimen panel, live readouts, "Inside the experiment" notes).

The specimen:
- A chubby plush baby dragon sitting on a table, all made from one signed distance field.
- Minky body: a big round head with a short snout and two felt horns, a pale belly quilted in horizontal bands, stubby arms, round haunches with padded feet and tiny felt claws.
- A tail curled round to one side, ending in a soft spade.
- A row of flat felt spikes down the head, back and tail.
- Face: glossy bead eyes, blushing cheeks, embroidered nostrils, a stitched smile with one little felt fang.
- Two quilted plush wings sewn on at the shoulders.

Physics:
- Body: XPBD soft body on a hex-cell lattice (co-rotational shape matching plus tetrahedral volume), 60 Hz, 6 substeps. Gravity and floor friction; the seat keeps its footing and the toy slowly rights itself like a weighted plush.
- Muscles instead of forces: the belly breathes (cells' rest shapes and rest volumes swell); the tail wags by lengthening cells on one side of its centre line and shortening them on the other, faster when the dragon is happy.
- Wings:
- each wing is a small XPBD cloth cut from a curved fan-shaped 3D pattern (stretch, shear and bend links), its two root rows embedded in the body lattice;
- a pose (fold back about the vertical, flap about a hinge along the body, both riding a shoulder frame from embedded points) pulls every point toward its target: firmly at the root, barely at the edge, so the stuffed wings lag and flop;
- collider spheres riding the body keep the wings off it.
- Flapping: downstrokes lift the dragon with a hover controller (about 6 cm off the table, bobbing with each beat), then it drops back onto its seat.
- Pulling a wing past its slack tows the body by that shoulder.

Rendering:
- Shell fur (base + N instanced shells, alpha-to-coverage under 4× MSAA): fur lie carried by the deformation gradient, damped-spring tip lag, Kajiya–Kay highlights, velvet sheen, a comb tool.
- Regions painted in rest space: belly with quilting seams, short-nap felt horns and spikes in the wing colour, padded soles, cheeks, smile groove.
- Wings drawn each frame as stuffed slabs swept from the cloth:
- a rolled leading edge in the body colour;
- three panels puffed between stitched ribs;
- a scalloped trailing edge;
- a shorter pile of the same minky.
- Glossy eyes, embroidery thread, felt fang and claws.
- Soft PCSS key-light shadows, contact occlusion on the studio floor, Khronos PBR Neutral tone mapping.
- NaN-safe WGSL (clamped pow/smoothstep, clamped post).

Interaction:
- Hand: lift and squash the dragon, or grab a wing to stretch it open (pull harder to tow the dragon).
- Finger: a finger reaches in from the viewer; poke to dent the stuffing; hold it pressed in to tickle — the dragon giggles, its wings shiver and its tail wags.
- Comb: brush the pile.
- Buttons: Flap, Stretch (wings spread wide), Boop (a sneeze: head bobs back, wings flare), Toss, Smooth fur, Reset.
- Sliders: Stuffing, Pile, Wingbeat.
- Palettes: Mint (lilac wings), Ember (coral with gold wings), Dusk (lavender with pink wings).
- Readouts: mass, volume % of rest, live wingspan in cm, lift off the table in cm.
- Orbit and zoom; responsive stacked layout on phones; adaptive quality; reduced-motion support.

title: Jelly pufferfish browser comparison
author: vib3coded
prompt:
Build an interactive 3D jelly pufferfish (fugu) as a single self-contained HTML page using three.js from a CDN.

The fish is a soft-body gummy sitting on a table. Model the body as one closed icosphere-topology skin with two rest shapes per vertex: a calm fish (blunt round head, body tapering to a short tail stalk, slightly flattened belly) and a fully inflated ball (sphere with the same tail stalk sticking out). Blend between them with an "inflation" value. Simulate with XPBD at a fixed 1/600 s substep (frame-rate independent): edge-length constraints, a global volume constraint, a soft global shape-matching pull toward the blended rest shape (rotation via polar decomposition, gently leaning upright), ground collision with friction, and damping applied to the wobble (velocity relative to the body's mean) so it jiggles but settles in about a second. Render with one Loop-subdivision pass for a smooth surface.

Behaviour: tapping the fish startles it. It gulps air three times (mouth opens on each gulp, small overshoot) until it is a round ball, stays puffed about 4 seconds, then slowly deflates while blowing iridescent bubbles from its mouth. Dragging grabs and stretches the jelly locally; dragging empty space orbits the camera; wheel or pinch zooms.

Details: ~260 soft spines that lie flat and hidden when calm, pop up one by one (staggered) as it inflates, wobble on their own springs, bend against the table, and lift the ball so it stands on its spines. Big glossy eyes (gold-green iris, large pupil, white catchlight) that follow the cursor. Puckered lips with a tiny white beak. Translucent ray-striped fins: fluttering pectorals, swaying tail fan, rippling dorsal and anal fins, all faster when alarmed. Dark freckles on the back, pale belly, a few air bubbles trapped inside the jelly.

Look: MeshPhysicalMaterial with transmission, clearcoat and sheen for a candy-gummy look; a soft environment map; a soft colored shadow with a faint caustic on a floor that matches the page background. Flavour presets Yuzu, Ramune, Momo, Matcha. Editorial "Material Studies" layout: big italic serif title "Fugu Jelly.", a side panel with flavour swatches, Firmness and Wobble sliders, Startle / Calm / Reset buttons, ¼ speed and Sound toggles, and live readouts for volume, spine angle and mood. Synthesized WebAudio sounds for gulps, a boing on tap, a hiss while deflating and tiny bubble pops. Responsive down to phone width.

title: Jelly lego bricks model comparison
author: semichenkko
prompt:
Build a single self-contained HTML file: an interactive 3D toy called "Jelly Bricks" - translucent gummy candy bricks you can grab, stretch, stack into a tower and knock over. Use three.js (import from a CDN) and any lightweight physics library you like. Everything must run by opening the file in a browser.

LOOK
- Bricks are classic stud-on-top building bricks (2x1, 2x2, 3x2, 4x2) in red, orange, yellow, green and blue. No brand names or logos anywhere.
- Material must read as real gummy candy: glossy, translucent, light passing through, deeper colour where the brick is thicker, soft rounded edges and rounded studs. Use MeshPhysicalMaterial with transmission, thickness, attenuation colour, clearcoat, and an environment map for reflections.
- Soft shadows plus a faint coloured glow on the floor under each brick, tinted by its colour.
- Clean white background, slight slow camera drift so the scene feels alive.

JELLY BEHAVIOUR (most important)
- Grab a brick and it stretches toward the cursor before it lifts off, like pulling taffy. Release it and the stretch snaps back with a decaying wobble.
- A brick lagging behind the cursor tilts slightly in the direction it's moving.
- Every landing squashes the brick flat, then it springs back up with a few wobbles (spring-damper squash and shear, done in the vertex shader).
- Dropping a brick on the stack snaps it in place, and the whole tower sways like pudding: each brick's wobble shifts the bricks above it, so the top moves the most.
- Pulling a brick out of the middle of the tower collapses it: the bricks above tumble, bounce off the floor and each other, and scatter a little - lively, not explosive.

UI (minimal editorial style)
- Top left: small caps label "Nº 09 / SOFT GOODS", big serif italic title "Jelly / Bricks." with "Bricks." in red, and a one-line subtitle.
- Floating panel on the right: flavor colour swatches, a "Wobble" slider that controls jelly softness, live "Stack height" and "Bricks" counters, and a black "Pour more bricks" button that drops a handful of new bricks from above with random spin.
- Bottom left hint: "Grab to lift · Drop to snap · Space to wobble". Space shakes the tower.
- Custom round cursor that shrinks while holding a brick.

Start with one 4x2 brick in the centre as the tower base and about 9 bricks scattered around it. Keep it at 60fps on a laptop.

title: Pokemon-themed UI states in a seamless beat-grid loop
author: TheGrootDev
prompt:
<inputs>
Ask me for: my featured Pokémon or starter trio, 8–12 Pokémon-themed UI states, and a royalty-free song around 120 BPM with a playful adventure or electronic feel. Confirm that the song’s license permits the intended use.Default palette: warm off-white, black, and Poké Ball red. Pokémon artwork keeps its original colors.
</inputs>

<direction>
A Pokémon-inspired UI motion film with Dribbble-level polish. Imagine a beautifully designed modern Pokédex: playful, precise, and instantly http://recognizable.One shape, never cut: a Poké Ball continuously morphs into every interface component by changing its size, radius, and color. Its central button, dividing line, and outer shell become the controls and structure of each new state. Content swaps with a short blur and carefully separated enter/exit timing.

A visible cursor drives every interaction with clicks, drags, and hover gestures. Use a light warm-gray canvas, clean Geist typography, consistent icon strokes, and crisp Pokémon artwork.

Use tightly damped springs with only a tiny overshoot. The camera smoothly reframes each state so the interface stays large and readable. The ending returns exactly to the opening Poké Ball for a seamless loop.

Banned: excessive bouncing, particle bursts, glows, gradients on UI chrome, mismatched icon strokes, dead time, generic dashboard layouts, abrupt scene changes, and unrelated floating elements.
</direction>

<structure>
120 BPM, 4/4 time, 7 bars: 28 beats, approximately 14 seconds. Something intentional happens on every http://beat.Bar 1 — Poké Ball activation

1. A closed Poké Ball sits centered; the cursor approaches.
2. The cursor clicks its central button.
3. The button becomes a circular scanning loader.
4. The scan resolves into a check, and the shell stretches into a compact Pokédex.

Bar 2 — Pokémon discovery
5. The Pokédex expands to reveal the featured Pokémon.
6. Its name, number, and type appear in a quick stagger.
7. The cursor clicks the cry/play control.
8. The control morphs into pause while a compact waveform animates.

Bar 3 — Trainer controls
9. The waveform flattens into a volume slider.
10. The cursor drags its Poké Ball-shaped knob to maximum.
11. Dragging beyond maximum elastically stretches the slider.
12. On release, it settles and compresses into a shiny-mode toggle.

Bar 4 — Pokémon details
13. The cursor flips shiny mode; the artwork changes to the correct shiny variant.
14. The toggle knob stretches into a liquid tab indicator.
15. The cursor selects “Stats.”
16. The card opens into a clean Pokémon stat chart.

Bar 5 — Stats to search
17. Stat bars draw themselves in sync with the beat.
18. The cursor hovers over a bar; a readable tooltip appears.
19. The chart retracts into the same container.
20. The container compresses into a Pokédex search field.

Bar 6 — Find and select
21. The search field expands into a command palette.
22. A short Pokémon name is typed; matching results filter.
23. The cursor selects a result, revealing its miniature artwork and type.
24. Enter confirms; the palette folds into an “Added to team” toast.

Bar 7 — Return to the Poké Ball
25. The toast’s confirmation mark becomes the Poké Ball’s central button.
26. The toast contracts; its edges become the circular shell.
27. The red upper half, white lower half, and black dividing line settle into place.
28. The cursor returns along a smooth path, matching the opening position and velocity as the loop wraps.

Use the chosen Pokémon consistently throughout. Keep visible text brief enough to read at this pace.
</structure>

<build>
1. Build one self-contained HTML file with a square 1440×1440 composition. Compute every animated style from time inside seek(t): no CSS transitions, timers, or state carried between frames.
2. Keep one persistent outer element throughout the sequence. Its internal artwork, labels, and controls may change, but the main silhouette must visibly connect every state.
3. Use closed-form spring step responses. For repeated target changes, sum one spring response per change so animation remains a pure function of time.
4. Give the tab indicator’s two edges different springs so the leading edge stretches ahead of the trailing edge. Apply the same technique to the toggle knob.
5. Make drags direct manipulation: while held, values follow cursor position. On release, use a closed-form spring matching the release position and velocity.
6. Analyze the supplied song with numpy to estimate the beat grid, verify the downbeat, and align the sequence. If the tempo differs from 120 BPM, adapt the timing to the actual music.
7. Use licensed UI sounds and align their measured transient peaks with clicks, confirmations, and morph accents.
8. Render with Playwright at four subframes per output frame. Blend each group of four with ffmpeg into a 60fps video for motion blur.
9. Render one preview frame per beat before the full video. Fix anything cramped, unreadable, visually disconnected, or off the beat grid.
10. Package artwork and fonts inside the HTML so rendering does not depend on network requests.
</build><gotchas>
Never put will-change on anything the camera scales; text can become blurry.Give outgoing and incoming content separate timing so labels never overlap during a morph.

Use accurate Pokémon artwork, names, types, shiny colors, and stats. Do not invent variants or stretch character artwork when the container changes shape.

Keep the main container recognizable through every transition. Pokémon artwork is content inside the morphing interface, not a replacement for the persistent shape.

Match the loop boundary exactly: geometry, content, camera, cursor position, and cursor velocity. Export the interval [0, duration) without duplicating the endpoint frame. Make the audio loop cleanly too.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for the inputs, then show me the proposed Pokémon state list on the 28-beat grid before writing any code.
</start>

title: OBLT e-bike: cinematic product header with an X-ray spotlight
author: iamtanzil_
prompt:
# OBLT E-bike Header

A full-viewport, dark, cinematic e-bike product header for the brand **OBLT**, built in React (client component) with pure CSS and an interactive cursor-following "x-ray" spotlight reveal — moving the mouse wipes away the bike's exterior photo to expose its internal carbon/gearbox structure underneath. Built with React only (no animation libraries).

## Tech stack (libraries actually imported)
- React only — `useRef`, `useState`, and the `MouseEvent` type. No framer-motion, no GSAP, no icon library. All animation is hand-written CSS keyframes + an inline CSS `mask-image`.
- SVG icon (the CTA arrow) is hand-inlined, not from a library.

## Fonts & global styles
- Single Google font, imported inside a `<style>` block:
  ```
  @import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Almarai:wght@300;400;700;800&display=swap');
  ```
- Font stack: `"Almarai","Helvetica Neue",Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif`.
- `-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased`. `box-sizing: border-box` applied to the root and all descendants (scoped to `.vt-header`, never global).

## Section container
- Root `<header className="vt-header">` is the mouse-tracking element (handlers: `onMouseEnter`, `onMouseMove`, `onMouseLeave`).
- Styles: `position: relative; display: flex; flex-direction: column; min-height: 100vh; overflow: hidden; padding: 32px 56px 44px; background-color: #272727; color: #fff;`.
- Internal vertical flow: top nav, then a flex-grow spacer "stage", then bottom content pinned to the base.

## Structure, section by section

### 1. Reveal background (`.vt-bg`, absolute inset:0, z-index 0, pointer-events:none)
Three stacked layers:
- **Base exterior image** (`.vt-bg-img`): the full bike exterior photo, `object-fit: cover; object-position: center;`, fills the layer. `user-select:none`, `-webkit-user-drag:none`, `referrerPolicy="no-referrer"`.
- **X-ray layer** (`.vt-bg-xray`, z-index 1): contains the bike x-ray/internal image (same cover/center sizing). This layer is masked by a radial gradient driven by cursor position (see Animations). `will-change: -webkit-mask-image, mask-image;` and `transition: -webkit-mask-image .12s linear, mask-image .12s linear;`.
- **Veil overlay** (`.vt-bg-veil`, z-index 2): a vertical darkening gradient so text stays legible top & bottom:
  ```
  linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(39,38,38,.62) 0%, rgba(39,38,38,.10) 26%, rgba(39,38,38,.10) 60%, rgba(39,38,38,.82) 100%)
  ```

### 2. Top nav (`.vt-nav`, z-index 30)
- `display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr auto 1fr; align-items: center; gap: 24px;`.
- **Logo** (left, `.vt-logo`): text `OBLT` followed by a `.` span. `font-size: 28px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.5px; color: #E0E1CC;` (dot is also `#E0E1CC`).
- **Center menu** (`.vt-menu`, gap 40px): three links — `E-bikes`, `Features`, `Connect`. Each: `font-size: 16px; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: .3px; color: #E0E1CC; opacity: .85; transition: opacity .2s ease;` hover → opacity 1.
- **Right cluster** (`.vt-nav-right`, gap 18px): an uppercase explore link plus a hamburger button.
  - `.vt-explore` link text: `Explore the bike` — `font-size: 14px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 1.5px; text-transform: uppercase; color: #E0E1CC;` hover → opacity .65.
  - **Hamburger** (`.vt-burger`, hidden on desktop): 34×34px, three `#E0E1CC` bars 22×2px, radius 2px, gap 5px. On `.open`: bar 1 `translateY(7px) rotate(45deg)`, bar 2 `opacity:0`, bar 3 `translateY(-7px) rotate(-45deg)`. Transition `transform .25s ease, opacity .2s ease`.
- **Mobile dropdown** (`.vt-mobile-menu`, rendered only when `menuOpen`): absolutely positioned below the nav (`top:100%; margin-top:16px; z-index:40`), `background: rgba(20,19,19,.97); backdrop-filter: blur(10px); border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.1); border-radius: 16px; padding: 8px 18px;`. Links (`E-bikes`, `Features`, `Connect`, `Explore the bike`): `color:#E0E1CC; font-size:18px; padding:14px 4px; border-bottom:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.08)`; last link `border-bottom:none; font-weight:700`. Each link closes the menu on click.

### 3. Stage spacer (`.vt-stage`, z-index 30, `flex: 1 1 0%`)
- `display: flex; align-items: flex-start; justify-content: flex-end; padding-top: 22px;`. In the current markup it is an empty `aria-hidden` spacer (the `.vt-hint` pulsing-dot styles exist in CSS but the hint element is not rendered).
- (Reference: `.vt-hint` styled as an uppercase 11px/600 label with a 36px circle dot, `border:1px solid rgba(46,211,176,.5); color:#2ed3b1;` running `vtPulse 1.8s ease-in-out infinite`.)

### 4. Bottom content (`.vt-bottom`, z-index 30)
12-column grid: `grid-template-columns: repeat(12, 1fr); align-items: end; gap: 18px 32px;`.
- **Headline** (`.vt-headline`, `grid-column: 1 / span 8`): `<h1>` containing the word-stagger component. h1 style: `color: #E0E1CC; font-weight: 500; font-size: clamp(36px, 7vw, 116px); line-height: 0.85; letter-spacing: -0.07em; white-space: nowrap; margin:0;`. Text: **Ready For The Ride**.
- **Right block** (`.vt-right`, `grid-column: 9 / span 4; align-self: end; transform: translateY(22px);`):
  - Paragraph (verbatim): `An integrated gearbox, battery, and motor engineered in carbon and built to be seen. Every system, in the open.` Style: `font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.2; color: rgba(225,224,204,.7);` animates in via `vtFadeUp .8s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) both` with `animation-delay: .5s`.
  - **CTA button** (`.vt-cta`): label **Reserve yours** plus a circular arrow. Pill: `color:#000; background:#E0E1CC; border:none; border-radius:9999px; padding:6px 6px 6px 22px; font-size: clamp(14px, 1vw, 16px); font-weight:500; display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:10px;`. Animates via `vtFadeUp .8s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) both`, `animation-delay: .7s`. Hover → `gap: 14px`. Inner circle `.circ`: 40×40px, `border-radius:50%; background:#000;` containing the SVG (stroke `#E0E1CC`); on button hover `.circ` scales to `1.1` (`transition: transform .25s ease`).

## Assets (every URL)
- Exterior photo (base layer): `https://cdn.jiro.build/ARS/OBLT%20E%20Bike/bike-exterior.png`
- X-ray / internals photo (revealed layer): `https://cdn.jiro.build/ARS/OBLT%20E%20Bike/bike-xray-original.png`
- CTA arrow icon: inline SVG, 16×16, `viewBox="0 0 24 24"`, `stroke="currentColor"`, `stroke-width="2.2"`, round caps/joins, path:
  ```
  M5 12h14M13 6l6 6-6 6
  ```

## Animations

### Cursor "x-ray" spotlight (signature interaction)
- State: `hovering` (bool) and `pos` ({x,y} in px relative to the section's bounding rect). `handleMove` computes `e.clientX - rect.left`, `e.clientY - http://rect.top`.
- Constants: `RADIUS = 165` px (spotlight radius), `FEATHER = 45` px (soft edge). Inner fully-clear radius = `RADIUS - FEATHER` = 120px.
- The x-ray layer's `maskImage` / `WebkitMaskImage` is set inline. When hovering:
  ```
  radial-gradient(circle 165px at {x}px {y}px, #000 0, #000 120px, transparent 165px)
  ```
  When not hovering (collapsed to nothing):
  ```
  radial-gradient(circle 0px at 50% 50%, transparent 0, transparent 0)
  ```
- Mask transitions at `.12s linear` so the reveal trails the cursor smoothly. NOTE: in CSS `mask`, opaque (`#000`) areas KEEP the layer — so the circle reveals the x-ray image while the rest of that layer is hidden (showing the exterior beneath).

### Headline word pull-up (`WordsPullUp` component)
- Splits the headline on spaces; each word is an `inline-block` span (`margin-right: 0.22em`, last word 0). Each word animates `wpuUp` with `cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) both`, default `duration = 0.6s`, staggered by `delayStep = 0.08s` (`animationDelay: i * 0.08s`).
- Keyframes:
  ```
  @keyframes wpuUp { from { transform: translateY(20px); opacity: 0; } to { transform: translateY(0); opacity: 1; } }
  ```
- Optional superscript asterisk (`.wpu-ast`, `font-size:0.31em; vertical-align:top; top:0.15em; left:-0.05em;`) — not enabled here (`asterisk` defaults false).
- Respects `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` → `.wpu-word { animation: none; }`.

### Fade-up for right block (`vtFadeUp`)
```
@keyframes vtFadeUp { from { transform: translateY(20px); opacity: 0; } to { transform: translateY(0); opacity: 1; } }
```
Paragraph delay `.5s`, CTA delay `.7s`; both `.8s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) both`.

### Pulse (defined for hint dot)
```
@keyframes vtPulse { 0%,100%{transform:scale(1);opacity:.7} 50%{transform:scale(1.12);opacity:1} }
```
Applied `vtPulse 1.8s ease-in-out infinite`.

## Responsive
- **≤1000px**: padding `24px 28px 32px`; nav becomes `1fr auto` (logo + right); center `.vt-menu` and `.vt-explore` hidden; hamburger shown; `.vt-bottom` collapses to single column (`gap:16px`); headline & right span full width; `.vt-right` `transform:none; align-self:start; margin-top:4px; max-width:520px`.
- **≤600px**: padding `18px 20px 26px`; logo `font-size:22px`; headline `white-space:normal; font-size: clamp(40px, 13vw, 72px); line-height:0.92`; paragraph `font-size:15px; margin-bottom:16px`; CTA `font-size:14px; padding:5px 5px 5px 20px`; `.circ` 36×36px.

## Key design principles
- Dark stage (`#272727`) with a single warm-cream accent (`#E0E1CC`) and a teal accent (`#2ed3b1`) reserved for the (optional) pulse hint.
- The product reveal IS the hero: cursor acts as an x-ray torch over a layered photo pair.
- Editorial oversized headline (line-height 0.85, tight `-0.07em` tracking) anchored bottom-left; supporting copy + CTA bottom-right.
- Staggered, eased (`cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)`) entrance for hierarchy.

## Common mistakes to avoid
- Don't invert the mask logic: opaque `#000` in the radial gradient REVEALS the x-ray layer; the transparent ring hides it. Getting this backwards shows internals everywhere except under the cursor.
- Keep `RADIUS - FEATHER` (120px) as the inner solid stop and `RADIUS` (165px) as the transparent stop — that 45px band is the soft feather.
- Mouse coordinates must be relative to the section rect (`getBoundingClientRect`), not the viewport.
- Mask transition is `.12s linear` only — a longer/eased transition makes the spotlight feel laggy.
- `white-space: nowrap` on the headline is intentional on desktop; only switch to `normal` at ≤600px.
- Scope all resets and the Almarai `@import` to the component; do not touch global `body`/`html`.

## Page title
OBLT — Ready For The Ride

## Integration (build-safety — do not skip)
- Add this section as a **new** component file with a unique name. Don't edit or overwrite any existing file except to add its import and render it.
- Render it **after** all existing sections; keep every previously built section exactly as-is — never replace or remove them.
- If no project exists, create a minimal React + Tailwind app; if one exists, use it as-is — don't re-scaffold or change the Tailwind/build config or version.
- Keep it self-contained: scope its fonts and any resets to this section; never set global `body`/`html`/`*` styles or a global font.
- Install only the libraries this section names.

title: Prompt bar to preview window: one continuous UI transformation
author: 0xnicc0
prompt:
<inputs>
Ask me for: a one-word product name for the wordmark, one accent color, and a royalty-free track around 120 BPM (e.g. Mixkit, free for commercial use).
</inputs>

<direction>
Product-launch UI motion in one continuous take. One shape tells the whole story: a prompt bar becomes a button, the button becomes a progress ring, the ring becomes a preview window, the window fills the screen, then shrinks into a toast and back into the prompt bar. No cuts, no fades between scenes: objects transform. A cursor triggers every change with real clicks. Warm off-white canvas, black UI, one accent color, Inter for UI and the wordmark. Springs everywhere with only a slight overshoot. Zoom the camera so each moment fills the square.
Banned: crossfades, gradients on UI, particles, glows, bouncy easing, dead beats, anything that feels like a template.
</direction>

<structure>
120 BPM, 24 beats, something happens on every beat.
Type the request into the prompt bar → click send → the bar collapses into a black circle → a progress ring fills in four steps while four chips spring out (concept, storyboard, motion, sound) → the chips fly into a timeline and the circle becomes a preview window → a playhead sweeps the clips → inside the preview an orbit draws itself, a planet starts moving and the wordmark rises letter by letter from a mask line → the preview fills the screen → the letters drop away, the planet flies into a toast and becomes its checkmark → "Rendered in code · 60 fps" → the toast turns back into an empty prompt bar. Last frame = first frame.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML file with a 1440x1440 canvas. Draw everything inside seek(t): no CSS transitions, timers or state carried between frames.
2. Use closed-form spring step responses. When a value changes target several times, add one spring per change so it stays a pure function of time.
3. The main shape is one rounded rect whose width, height, radius, position and color are each a chain of springs.
4. Typing is derived from time: characters shown = floor(progress × length), with a caret that blinks only when idle.

Beats 22-34: the casting stage. A crowd of black and white portraits in an arc, a 3D stage block, and the creators gliding through like a carousel. Each plays live in a big disc in black and white, with their name in pink on the stage, their followers, and a MATCH % that counts up. One beat later a "CAST ✓" stamp lands and the clip fades to colour. A counter rolls 1/4 to 4/4.
Beats 34-39: pink floods out of the last disc. The disc morphs into a phone screen (the clip keeps playing) and fans into 4 phones playing all 4 creators, with views counting up. "4 ADS" and "BY FRIDAY" rise.

</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML canvas. Every frame is a pure function of time inside seek(t).
2. A beat map in beats, B = 60/BPM, with the song placed so its drop lands on beat 8.
3. The 3D box is an orthographic projection: each face is a 1440px offscreen canvas drawn with an affine transform and shaded by its normal.
4. Cut the clips to 30fps JPEG sequences with ffmpeg, draw frame floor(t*30), and do the black and white with ctx.filter.

A layer whose background is a huge flood circle still covers the screen after sliding down one frame height, so switch it to a full-frame rect once it has flooded. Counters read the frame's time, not the subframe's. The disc must morph inside the same camera transform as the scene it leaves, or it jumps.

title: Escape the Orbit: a tracked phrase becomes a kinetic speech
author: Gdgtify
prompt:
Create a 20.00-second kinetic typography film titled “ESCAPE THE ORBIT,” based on John F. Kennedy’s Rice University address, September 12, 1962.

The central experience: a sentence discovers that it can change its own trajectory.

Deliver one complete, self-contained HTML file. Composition: 1080×1080. Target: 60fps. Use Canvas, SVG, or embedded WebGL. Embed required assets and libraries. The film must work without audio.

EXACT DISPLAY TEXT
“We choose to go to the moon”
“[…]”
“not because they are easy,”
“but because they are hard”
Preserve this order. The bracketed ellipsis explicitly indicates omitted speech. Attribution is separate from the excerpt. No additional slogans.
ART DIRECTION
Background: midnight # 080D23.
Primary type: warm white # FFF4DD.
Trajectory: electric coral # FF654F.
Secondary orbital geometry: blue # 6685FF.
Use a broad, confident grotesque for the speech and a sharply drawn italic for the final emphatic word. Avoid the appearance of a spacecraft dashboard. No rockets, astronaut illustrations, starfield wallpaper, lens flares, or decorative telemetry.
The frame should resemble an exceptionally refined astronomical instrument that has become expressive.

CENTRAL VISUAL RULE
The baseline of the sentence is a trajectory.

At first it is trapped in a closed orbit. A rhetorical decision changes that orbit into an open path. The letters remain the same travelers throughout.
Use an abstract orbital metaphor; do not present invented mission data or imply a physically accurate flight simulation.
STORYBOARD
0.00–3.50
The opening excerpt appears across the center, large and horizontal. Reveal it in three meaningful phrase groups.
A single hairline ellipse passes behind the baseline. A small circular lunar mark occupies its distant focus.
Hold the completed phrase motionless for 700ms.

3.50–6.00
The camera pulls back. The previously straight baseline reveals a shallow curvature.

The phrase travels along the ellipse as a coherent unit. Keep its glyphs upright during the initial movement. Only after the reading hold may they progressively adopt the tangent of the path.

The viewer realizes the sentence is circling rather than advancing.
6.00–7.00
Show the bracketed omission in an uncluttered central opening. The orbital movement decelerates.

7.00–10.50
Reveal the next clause on the near side of the orbit. Its final word travels through one smooth, effortless arc and returns toward where it started.

This ease should feel elegant but unproductive. Avoid comic bouncing.

10.50–14.50
Reveal the final clause horizontally before transforming it.
At its emphasis, the ellipse opens at one precise point. The same tracked letter group takes the new tangent and departs.
Perform one deliberate 70-degree camera roll. Counter-rotate the active phrase so it remains readable while the orbital field changes orientation around it.

The trajectory sweeps from lower left to upper right. Acceleration is conveyed by expanding spacing between its trailing marks, not by shaking the camera.

14.50–17.00
The camera matches the departing phrase’s velocity. The phrase becomes visually still while the old orbit recedes beneath it.

The lunar mark enlarges into a restrained crescent through geometric overlap. The crescent brackets the destination without becoming a cartoon illustration.
17.00–20.00
Resolve into a spacious editorial composition containing the selected excerpt in reading order, including its omission marker.

The open trajectory runs through the margins and exits the frame. Hold the entire image completely still for the final 1.2 seconds.

CHOREOGRAPHY
Use only three camera operations: pullback, roll, velocity match.
Give each operation a rhetorical purpose.
Keep the currently read phrase at least 64px high in the 1080px composition.
Motion blur may affect trailing geometry, never the active text.
No word may begin its ornamental travel before its reading hold finishes.

IMPLEMENTATION
Represent the ellipse and departure path analytically. Blend position and tangent continuously at the departure point; no teleportation.
Use arc-length sampling for consistent spacing along curves.
Separate camera transforms from glyph orientation.
Cache glyph rendering and static geometry.
Expose window.ready and window. seek(t). Seeking must pause playback and render any time from 0 through 20 deterministically, including out-of-order calls.
Provide window.frame(n) for n=0…1199 at t=n/60.
Render t=20 as the final held composition.
Use no accumulated physics or runtime randomness.

QUALITY GATE
Inspect frames at 0, 3, 5, 7.5, 10.5, 13, 16, and 19 seconds.
Verify that the same tracked phrase visibly follows its own trajectory.

title: Tesla Roadster SpaceX Rocket Launch in Three.js
author: olezhavich
prompt:
GOAL:
Create a highly detailed, cinematic, interactive 3D scene in Three.js where a futuristic Tesla Roadster launches from a massive rocket launch complex using reaction thrusters. The result should feel like a premium CGI spectacle with realistic materials, detailed geometry, impressive lighting, rich atmospheric effects, and smooth camera choreography.
CORE CONCEPT:
What if Tesla launched the next-generation Roadster like a SpaceX rocket? The car sits on a launch platform, secured by mechanical hold-down clamps. Warning lights flash, vapor builds, thrusters ignite, clamps release, and the Roadster rises into a controlled hover before accelerating into the sky. This is a cinematic concept, not a realistic engineering simulation.

CAR DESIGN:
Create a highly recognizable next-generation Tesla Roadster using the provided reference images. Match its silhouette, proportions, front fascia, headlights, body curves, roofline, wheels, and overall appearance as closely as possible. Use detailed geometry, premium automotive paint, realistic-looking glass, metallic materials, and convincing reflections. Avoid generic sports car shapes or overly simplistic geometry. The Roadster must remain clearly visible throughout the important stages.
LAUNCH COMPLEX:
Build a massive modern rocket launch facility with a tall launch tower, industrial gantry structures, service platforms, mechanical hold-down clamps, support arms, railings, stairs, pipes, floodlights, warning lights, vapor vents, and distant infrastructure. The environment should feel large, believable, and highly detailed. Choose a dramatic coastal, industrial, or desert setting with cinematic atmospheric lighting.

AUTOMATIC ANIMATION:
The entire sequence must start automatically when the page loads, without clicking anything. No intro screen, blank scene, or long waiting period. The first frame must already look impressive, and interesting motion should begin within the first 1–3 seconds.
ANIMATION SEQUENCE:

Hero Reveal: Begin with a cinematic shot of the Roadster on the launch platform. The camera moves smoothly while warning lights flash, vapor drifts, and industrial lighting illuminates the vehicle.
Pre-Launch: Increase atmospheric tension with smoke, pressure vents, mechanical movements, subtle vibration, and gradually intensifying thruster illumination.

Ignition: Activate the thrusters with bright exhaust, expanding smoke, particles, reflections, and lighting effects interacting with the surrounding structures.
Clamp Release: The mechanical hold-down clamps must visibly unlock, rotate, and retract away from the car. Animate their actual 3D components rather than making them disappear.

Hover: The Roadster lifts slightly above the platform and remains suspended briefly. Thrusters continue firing while smoke, dust, and lighting react beneath the vehicle. Make this moment dramatic and clearly visible.

Liftoff: The Roadster accelerates vertically past the launch tower. The camera smoothly follows the car, emphasizing scale, speed, and the power of the propulsion system.

Final Shot: Transition to a wide cinematic view showing the Roadster climbing into the sky, leaving an atmospheric exhaust trail above the launch complex.

TIMELINE:
Aim for an approximately 18–22 second cinematic sequence. Use the first 3 seconds for the hero shot and buildup, seconds 3–5 for ignition and clamp release, seconds 5–8 for hover, seconds 8–15 for ascent, and the remaining time for a dramatic final shot. Synchronize all mechanical movements, lighting changes, particles, vehicle motion, and camera animation. Use time-based animation for smooth playback.

CAMERA & LIGHTING:
Create professional cinematic camera movements, including establishing shots, slow orbits, close-ups, low-angle hero shots, hover tracking, and ascent-following shots. Keep the Roadster readable and avoid chaotic camera movements. Use dramatic sunrise, blue-hour, or nighttime lighting with industrial floodlights, realistic-looking reflections, atmospheric haze, and thruster illumination.

VISUAL EFFECTS:
Include detailed smoke plumes, pressure vapor, exhaust particles, dust, atmospheric mist, glowing thrusters, subtle heat distortion, environmental reflections, and tasteful bloom or post-processing. Effects should feel connected to the action rather than purely decorative. Smoke and lighting must react convincingly to the launch without obscuring the vehicle.

INTERACTION:
Autoplay is the priority, but optional controls may include replay, pause/resume, slow motion, camera switching, and free orbit. Keep the interface minimal and visually clean. The scene must be fully functional without any manual interaction.

TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS:
Use Three.js, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. You may use suitable open-source assets, libraries, custom shaders, particle systems, and post-processing to improve quality. Organize the project into multiple files if needed. Optimize for smooth real-time rendering and make sure it runs locally in a modern browser. This must be a real interactive 3D experience, not a prerecorded video. Test the completed scene and fix major visual or functional issues.

IMPORTANT FOR RECORDING:
The scene should be ready to record immediately after refreshing the page. Prioritize a powerful first frame, continuous animation, clearly visible mechanical movements, impressive hover and liftoff moments, and a satisfying cinematic ending. Avoid unnecessary delays or static sections.

title: Night Tokyo: Rainy Vending Machine 3D Diorama
author: sprinntt
prompt:
Build an interactive 3D web demo: **"Night Tokyo — Vending Machine"**.

A single Japanese vending machine standing alone on a rainy Tokyo street at night, presented as a small floating diorama. It is part of a series of minimal "Night Tokyo" miniatures, so the look matters more than the feature count: one object, rich materials, light and motion you want to keep watching.

## Deliverable
- One self-contained `index.html` in the current folder. Open it and it works: no build step, no server-only features.
- Three.js only, loaded from a CDN via an import map with an exact pinned version. Official Three.js addons (postprocessing, controls, etc.) are fine. No other libraries.
- No external assets: no image textures, models, fonts or audio files. Everything is procedural (geometry, canvas textures, shaders, Web Audio).

## The scene
- A cut-out slab of street (about 3×3 m) floating in darkness: wet asphalt with puddles and a strip of curb/sidewalk. The cut edges show a cross-section (asphalt layers, maybe a drain). Beyond the slab: darkness and falling rain.
- The vending machine is the main light source: a glowing front with two or three rows of drinks behind glass, a round selection button under each drink, a small price display, a coin/IC-card panel, and the pickup flap at the bottom. Fictional drink brands only; Japanese labels are welcome. At most one small prop next to it (e.g. a recycling bin for cans).
- Rain: streaks visible in the machine's light, ripples in the puddles.
- Wet ground: convincing reflections of the glowing machine and its colors in the asphalt and puddles. This is the key shot.
- Palette: deep blue-black night, warm white machine light, a few saturated accents from the drinks and buttons. Subtle bloom is fine; don't wash everything out.
- Small signs of life: e.g. the fluorescent tube occasionally flickers, the rain intensity varies slightly. Rare, small, believable.

## Interaction
- Hovering a selection button lights it up.
- Clicking buys the drink: the price display reacts, a mechanical sound plays, the can drops inside the machine, the pickup flap swings open and the can rolls out onto the wet pavement, settling with a believable bounce and roll. It stays there. Repeated purchases leave several cans on the ground (cap the count for performance and remove the oldest gracefully).
- Each drink has limited stock (e.g. 3). When it runs out, its 売切 (sold out) light turns on and the button no longer dispenses.
- Sound, synthesized with Web Audio: rain ambience, button click, can drop, can rolling on asphalt. Audio starts after the first user interaction. `M` toggles mute.
- Camera: a strong default 3/4 shot at roughly eye level, with the machine filling most of the frame height, and a slow, subtle idle drift. Drag to orbit within limited angles, scroll to zoom within limits. `C` resets to the default shot.

## Quality bar
- Must look good at any aspect ratio, including narrow ones (around 8:9 and 9:16): it will be recorded side by side with another version.

## How to work
Work autonomously and don't ask clarifying questions; where something is unspecified, make the choice you think looks best. If your environment lets you open the page and look at it, do so and iterate on the visuals until you are happy with them. When finished, stop and briefly list what you built.

title: Interactive 3D Snow Globe Comparison
author: shmopixbzn
prompt:
Build "Snow Globe": a premium interactive 3D snow globe holding a tiny winter village, where every shake leaves a lasting, softly accumulating snowfall.
The emotional goal is the hush after shaking a real snow globe: "I want to shake it again and watch it settle."
ART DIRECTION
A heavy glass sphere rests on a turned walnut base on a warm linen tabletop. Inside: three cottages with steep roofs, a small chapel, a cluster of pines, a frozen pond and a lamppost. Use a palette of cream, frosted blue, pine green, brick red and warm window amber.
The glass should feel real: subtle refraction at the edges, a soft window-shaped highlight, a faint reflection of the room. Snow flakes are small, slightly irregular discs, not uniform dots. Accumulated snow is soft, rounded and matte.
CORE INTERACTION
Drag the globe to tilt and shake it.
Fast motion lifts settled snow into a swirling cloud.
Release to let the snow drift and settle.
Repeated shakes redistribute snow; gentle ones lift only the top layer.
The globe must follow the pointer closely, with a slight weighty lag. On phones, optional device-motion shaking after explicit permission.
THE SETTLING
Snow inherits the swirl of the liquid: it keeps circling, slows, and falls in lazy spirals. It accumulates as visible layers on roofs, branches, the lamppost cap and the pond. Thick snow slides off steep roofs in small clumps. The village lights glow brighter as the snow quiets.
Avoid snow passing through objects, sudden popping into place, or flat uniform coverage.
SOUND AND ATMOSPHERE
Optional sound: a soft liquid slosh linked to shake velocity, a faint glassy shimmer as snow falls, and a very distant chapel bell when everything has settled. Audio starts only after explicit activation. The scene must feel complete in silence.
TECHNICAL APPROACH
Use Three.js. Simulate the liquid as a simple damped swirl field driven by globe velocity. Store accumulation in a heightfield or per-surface snow map so it persists and builds. Keep the particle count modest and stable; reuse particles instead of creating new ones.
Keep the camera stationary while shaking; allow a restrained orbit when idle.
PRESENTATION
Show "Snow Globe", the hint "Shake gently. Watch it settle.", and discreet reset and sound controls.
Start with a light snowfall already drifting down so the scene is alive on arrival. No introduction modal.
DELIVERY AND PRIORITIES
Deliver a complete runnable browser experience with procedural geometry and textures and mouse/touch support. First perfect the shake-and-settle feel, then accumulation, then glass rendering and small details. Verify repeated shakes, full settling, reset, and stable performance on mobile. Include setup instructions.

title: Interactive 3D Squishy Toast Memory Foam Simulation
author: semichenkko
prompt:
Build "Squishy Toast" - a single self-contained HTML file (three.js from a CDN is the only dependency): an interactive 3D slice of slow-rise memory foam bread you can press, poke, stretch and squash.

The toast
- A real bread silhouette: square body, rounded "muffin top" crown, soft beveled edges
- Crumb face: warm cream color, procedural pores of varied size with highlights and a bump map, a toasted golden edge fading in toward the center
- Crust: golden-brown with subtle grain and a light sheen

Physics (this is the whole point - it must feel like foam, not geometry)
- Densely tessellated mesh deformed per vertex every frame, normals recomputed
- Press and hold: a smooth gaussian dent, crumb bulges outward around the rim, the bottom stays planted on the table
- Release: the dent rises back slowly and exponentially, like memory foam, with no instant snap. A faint elastic ripple runs across the crumb after release
- Several dents can coexist, each recovering on its own
- Grab the crust and pull: the bread stretches elastically, thins as it stretches, then springs back with a damped wobble
- Palm squash: the whole slice flattens and barrel-bulges at mid-height, then breathes back up
- Drop: lift and release, squash-and-stretch on impact, small decaying bounce

Flavors
- Butter, strawberry jam (glossy clearcoat, deeper color), avocado (mashed texture). The spread sits on the crumb, leaves a crust rim and deforms with the bread

UI
- Editorial product-page style on a white background. Large italic serif title "Squishy / Toast.", a short subtitle, a minimal card on the right with flavor swatches, a softness slider (controls dent size and recovery time), a live "Rise" meter and a "Fresh slice" reset button

title: Interactive WebGPU Plush Hedgehog Simulation

prompt:

title: Hiking documentary: a narrated 3D route
author: shengtang135754
prompt:
请用 Three.js 写一个单文件 HTML（index.html），做一个"徒步纪实风格"的 3D 场景，用来录屏做解说视频。

【基本要求】
- Three.js 通过 CDN（cdnjs 或 jsdelivr）引入，不需要构建工具，浏览器双击即可运行。
- 画面严格 16:9，内部按 1920×1080 设计，窗口缩放时等比居中，黑边填充。
- 所有可调参数（地形种子、路线点、相机速度等）集中放在文件顶部的 CONFIG 对象里。

【地形】
- 用多层噪声（Simplex/Perlin，自己实现即可）生成一条南北走向的高山峡谷：两侧高山、中间谷底，谷底有一条蜿蜒的河道。
- 按高度和坡度上色：山脊深褐/灰、坡面土黄、谷底浅黄、河道蓝灰，山顶可有少量积雪。
- 加雾和平行光，营造高原干燥冷色调氛围。

【路线与人物】
- CONFIG 里用一组 (x, z) 路径点定义徒步路线，用 CatmullRomCurve3 生成平滑曲线并贴合地形高度。
- 路线渲染为醒目的红色粗线（带轻微发光），已走过部分亮红色，未走部分半透明。
- 一个红色低模小人（胶囊体+球头+红色外套即可）沿路线匀速行走，可设置速度，支持暂停。
- 支持在路线上放"事件标记点"（如集合点、失踪点），显示为带文字的立式标牌或脉冲圆圈。

【相机】
- 四种模式，数字键 1-4 切换，切换时平滑过渡：
  1. 高空俯瞰（沿路线前方飞行，微微倾斜）
  2. 跟随（人物斜后上方）
  3. 环绕（绕着人物缓慢旋转）
  4. 自由（鼠标拖动旋转，滚轮缩放，WASD 移动）
- 相机速度、高度、俯仰角可在 CONFIG 里调。

【界面叠加层（HTML/CSS）】
- 左右两侧各一列人物卡片：方形头像框（先用纯色+首字占位，可通过 CONFIG 换成图片 URL）、名字、身份小字。
- 人物状态：正常 / 遇难（卡片变灰并加红色边框）/ 失踪（卡片半透明并显示问号）。
- 底部居中大字幕区，白字黑描边，支持高亮关键词（用 [[关键词]] 标记，显示为黄色）。
- 右上角显示"第 X 集"标题和当前进度条（可选）。

【时间线驱动】
- 在 CONFIG 里用一个数组 TIMELINE 描述剧情，每项含 time（秒）和 action，例如：
  { time: 0,  action: "camera", mode: 1 }
  { time: 3,  action: "subtitle", text: "那你为什么还敢[[参加]]？", duration: 4 }
  { time: 8,  action: "walk", from: 0, to: 0.4 }       // 人物在路线上的进度 0~1
  { time: 15, action: "status", member: "胡杨林", state: "missing" }
  { time: 20, action: "marker", at: 0.6, text: "失踪点" }
- 播放逻辑：按 Space 开始/暂停，R 重置，时间到了自动触发对应事件。
- 页面左上角显示一个小的调试面板（当前时间、相机模式），按 H 一键隐藏所有调试和提示，录屏时保持画面干净。

【示例内容】
- 预置 8 位虚构队员（铁镐-组织者、千鸟、胡杨林、咪咪、队员5～8），一条约 90 秒的演示时间线，覆盖：开场俯瞰、行进、事件标记、人物状态变化、结尾字幕。

【代码要求】
- 代码清晰分区并加中文注释（地形、路线、人物、相机、UI、时间线）。
- 保证在普通笔记本上能稳定 30fps 以上，地形分辨率不要过高（约 256×256 顶点）。
- 完成后告诉我：如何修改路线、如何换头像、如何新增时间线事件。

title: Meteor Time-Freeze Cinematic Sequence Prompt Orchestrated by Opus 5.5
author: MadMax_Series
prompt:
「身份锁定｜女人」
成年女性，约二十八岁，黑色长直发，浅色皮肤，深棕色眼睛；身穿及膝的亮红色羊毛大衣、黑色牛仔裤、黑色短靴；亮红色大衣是画面中最醒目的颜色；全程同一人、同一服装，不换脸、不变装。

「身份锁定｜男人」
成年男性，约三十岁，深棕色短发，下巴有浅浅的胡茬，浅橄榄色皮肤；身穿深海军蓝夹克、灰色连帽衫、深色牛仔裤；开场双手各拿一杯白色纸杯咖啡（杯身无任何文字或标志）；全程同一人、同一服装，不换脸、不变装。

「空间」
固定地理：一条约十五米宽的双车道城市街道，两侧是带大玻璃橱窗的商店；街道左侧是一家亮着暖光的咖啡馆，玻璃门朝向街道；街道右侧正对着咖啡馆的是一个玻璃顶的公交车站；街道笔直延伸向远方，尽头是城市的地平线，陨石从画面右上方划向远方地平线，撞击发生在大街尽头的城外，尘墙从大街尽头沿街道朝镜头方向推进；他从左侧咖啡馆出来，她在右侧公交站，两人在街道中央相遇，左右关系全程不翻转；街上还有约十名行人。

「首帧」
24mm街道中央低位广角，朝向大街尽头，第一帧是安静的深夜街道：橱窗灯光、路灯、零星行人，夜空漆黑；此刻天空右上方已经开始泛起一片刺眼的橙白色光。

「时间轴 / SHOT 1」
0.0–4.0秒｜24mm街道低位广角，缓慢上仰：0.0–1.5秒天空在一瞬间由漆黑变得比白昼还亮，橙白色的强光照亮整条街，所有路灯、行人、停着的汽车的影子在路面上同时快速转动、扫过；1.5–3.0秒行人纷纷停下抬头，一颗山一样巨大的燃烧陨石拖着熊熊火焰与滚滚浓烟，从画面右上方划过夜空、飞向大街尽头的地平线，天空被它的火尾撕开；3.0–4.0秒陨石的强光在左侧咖啡馆的玻璃门上反射出一道耀眼的光斑，形成第一次动作匹配剪切。

「时间轴 / SHOT 2」
4.0–9.0秒｜从同一道玻璃门上的反射光斑切入，35mm手持在咖啡馆门外：4.0–5.5秒他推开玻璃门走出来，双手各拿一杯咖啡，抬头看见天空，脚步停住；5.5–7.0秒他低下头，目光穿过街道，看见对面公交站下穿红色大衣的她，她也正看着他，两人隔着街道对视；7.0–8.0秒两人同时迈步，冲向街道中央，他仍然攥着两杯咖啡；8.0–9.0秒大街尽头的地平线上爆出一团巨大的白光，白光瞬间吞没整个画面，形成第二次动作匹配剪切。

「时间轴 / SHOT 3」
9.0–15.0秒｜从同一团白光切入，35mm在街道中央略高处，朝大街尽头望去：9.0–11.0秒白光褪去，大街尽头的地平线上，一团橙红色的火光与蘑菇状尘云冲天而起；11.0–13.5秒冲击波沿着大街一路推来，两侧的橱窗从远到近一扇接一扇依次炸碎，玻璃向街心喷射，汽车警报响成一片，路边的汽车被推得晃动；一堵数十层楼高、内部翻滚着橙红火光的灰褐色尘墙沿着大街朝镜头方向席卷而来；他从画面左侧、她从画面右侧冲进画面，朝街心奔跑；13.5–15.0秒最近的一扇橱窗在镜头旁炸开，一大片玻璃碎片朝镜头飞来，形成第三次动作匹配剪切。

「时间轴 / SHOT 4」
15.0–19.0秒｜从同一片飞来的玻璃碎片切入，50mm侧面平视，两人位于街道中央，画面左侧是他、右侧是她，背景是逼近的尘墙：15.0–17.0秒两人相距只有三步，彼此伸出手，他松开双手，两杯咖啡翻滚着落下、咖啡泼溅而出，玻璃碎片在他们周围飞旋，尘墙已近在二十米外，她的头发和大衣被风压向后扬起；17.0秒一切骤然静止——空中的玻璃碎片、泼溅的咖啡、翻滚的纸杯、她扬起的头发、尘墙与其中的火焰、远处奔跑的行人全部定格在原位，没有任何运动；17.0–19.0秒整个画面完全静止，唯一的变化是她的眼睛缓缓眨了一下，形成第四次动作匹配剪切。

「时间轴 / SHOT 5」
19.0–25.0秒｜从同一双眨动的眼睛切入，35mm手持跟在她右肩后方：19.0–20.5秒她发现自己能动，缓缓环顾四周，她的头发和大衣随着她的动作重新垂下；20.5–23.5秒她小心地向前迈步，穿过成千上万片悬停在空中的玻璃碎片，碎片在橙红火光中闪烁；她用指尖轻轻推开挡在面前的一片玻璃，那片玻璃被推到旁边后就停在新的位置不再移动；她经过悬在半空的咖啡泼溅与翻滚中定格的纸杯、一只张开翅膀悬停在空中的鸽子、定格在奔跑姿势中的行人；尘墙像一道翻滚中被冻住的悬崖，火焰在其中凝固不动；23.5–25.0秒她走到定格的他面前，抬起右手伸向他的脸，形成第五次动作匹配剪切。

「时间轴 / SHOT 6」
25.0–30.0秒｜从同一只抬起的手切入，50mm两人侧面近景，背景是凝固的尘墙与悬停的玻璃：25.0–26.5秒她的指尖轻轻触碰到他定格的脸颊；26.5–28.0秒他眨了一下眼，胸口吸进一口气，眼珠转动，看向她——他也能动了；两人近在咫尺地对视，他抬手握住她的手；28.0–30.0秒就在他们身旁，一片悬停的玻璃碎片开始轻轻颤动，随后缓缓向下落去，两人同时转头看向那片下落的玻璃，画面在玻璃下落的过程中截断。

「物理」
陨石的强光真实地改变整条街的照明与影子方向；冲击波使橱窗按距离由远到近依次碎裂，玻璃从窗框向外喷射；尘墙是真实翻滚的灰尘与火焰体积；静止时刻是绝对的：除了她（以及之后的他）以外，一切物体保持在原位、原姿态，没有运动模糊、没有漂移；她推开的那片玻璃停留在被推到的新位置；静止前她头发和大衣被风扬起，她开始移动后，她身上的头发和衣物恢复受重力自然下垂；只有结尾那一片玻璃开始颤动并下落，其余一切仍保持静止；碎裂的橱窗、悬停的碎片与尘墙跨越所有剪切持续存在，绝不复原。

「镜头」
SHOT 1街道低位广角上仰揭示陨石，SHOT 2咖啡馆门外手持，SHOT 3街心略高处望向大街尽头看冲击波与尘墙，SHOT 4两人侧面平视直到定格，SHOT 5手持跟在她肩后穿过静止的世界，SHOT 6两人侧面近景；五次剪切都从上一个镜头结束时的同一元素切入（玻璃门反射光斑、白光、飞来的玻璃碎片、眨动的眼睛、抬起的手）；定格时刻摄影机也保持静止，只有在SHOT 5她移动时摄影机才跟随她移动；无慢动作、无英雄仰角、无胜利定格。

「光线/色彩」
开场深夜冷蓝色调与暖黄橱窗灯光；陨石出现后整条街被橙白色强光照亮、影子剧烈转动；冲击波与尘墙阶段为翻滚的橙红火光与灰褐尘雾；静止世界被尘墙内凝固的橙红火光从背后照亮，悬停的玻璃碎片反射出无数橙色光点；她的亮红色大衣始终是画面中最醒目的颜色。

「声音」
SHOT 1 <夜晚街道的安静车流、陨石划过天空的低沉轰鸣与空气撕裂声逐渐增强>；SHOT 2 <咖啡馆门铃与门被推开、他的脚步声、远方撞击的爆鸣>；SHOT 3 <冲击波的巨大轰响、橱窗依次爆碎、汽车警报连成一片、尘墙翻滚的低沉咆哮>；SHOT 4 <狂风与玻璃飞旋的声音在17秒戛然而止，变成完全的静止>；SHOT 5 <只有她的脚步踩在碎玻璃上的细响与她的呼吸，她推开玻璃时一声轻微的玻璃触碰声>；SHOT 6 <他吸进一口气的声音、两人的呼吸、那片玻璃开始颤动时细微的嗡嗡震响>。

「锁定」
严格六个镜头、五次动作匹配剪切；全片无对白、无人声说话；她的红色大衣与他的深蓝夹克全程不变，两人不换脸、不融合；静止后除了她、之后的他、以及结尾那一片玻璃以外，一切保持绝对静止、不漂移；碎裂的橱窗、悬停的玻璃碎片、定格的咖啡与鸽子、凝固的尘墙持续存在，绝不复原；每人两臂两腿、每手五指；全片保持真人实拍质感；结尾那片玻璃下落过程中画面截断。

title: Interactive WebGPU Plush Hammerhead Shark
author: vib3coded
prompt:
Build a single-file interactive WebGPU page called "Plush Hammerhead".

Page: an editorial layout with a big two-line title "Plush / Hammerhead.", a warm studio-grey background, a control panel on the right, live readouts and collapsible technical notes. English UI.

The toy: a plush hammerhead shark. It has a wide, flat hammer-shaped head (cephalofoil) whose ends sweep back a little, with a shallow notch at the middle of the front edge. A glass eye sits on each tip of the hammer, looking out sideways. It has a tall sickle-shaped dorsal fin, two pectoral fins and a tail with a long upper lobe and a small lower one. A cream belly panel is sewn on below a seam along each flank, with embroidered gill lines. A smiling mouth is cut in under the hammer, lined with felt and set with soft white felt teeth; its lower jaw swings open on a hinge.

Simulation:
- Body, hammer and fins are one signed distance field filled with a soft-body XPBD lattice: shape-matched hexahedral cells and tetrahedral volume preservation. It is skinned to a high-res surface-nets mesh.
- It swims with a travelling S-wave that bends the cells' rest shapes side to side, more toward the tail, and steers by turning its head, the body curving into each turn.
- Fur is drawn as alpha-to-coverage shells over minky pile. The pile lags behind each jiggle on a spring and can be combed.

Behaviour:
- It circles its space.
- Scan: it sweeps its hammer side to side over the floor the way real hammerheads hunt. It also does this on its own now and then, and a little while hunting.
- Feed drops in a felt fish: it turns, closes in faster, opens wide and snaps it up.
- Dash is a burst of fast tail beats; Chomp opens the mouth and snaps it shut.
- Grab it by the tail and it thrashes; let go and it shoots off.
- Boop the middle of the hammer with the finger and it wriggles and blushes.

Tools: Hand, Finger, Comb.

Controls:
- Buttons: Feed, Dash, Scan, Chomp, Smooth fur, Reset, Pause.
- Toggles: Circle, quarter speed, Mesh.
- Sliders: Stuffing, Pile, Tail beat.
- Three fabrics: Bronze, Lagoon, Sunset.
- Readouts: mass, volume, beats per minute, fish eaten.
- Phone layout with a stacked panel.

title: One-Tap Flying Mobile Game in HTML5 Canvas
author: bytwize
prompt:
Build a polished mobile game I can play in my phone's browser.

Concept: a one-tap flying game in the spirit of Flappy Bird, with its own original
character, art and name. Tap to flap, gravity pulls you down, fly through the gaps
between obstacles. Every gap you pass is +1 point. Hit anything and it's game over.

Requirements:
- One file: index.html with all HTML, CSS and JavaScript inline. No external
  libraries, images, fonts or audio files. Draw everything in code and make
  sounds with the Web Audio API.
- Built for phones in portrait. Fill the screen, respect safe areas, stay crisp on
  high-DPI screens. Tap anywhere to flap; also support mouse click and the space bar
  for desktop testing. No scrolling, zooming or text selection while playing.
- Screens: a start screen with the game's name and a "tap to start" hint, the game,
  and a game over screen with the score, the best score (saved in localStorage) and
  a restart button.
- Game feel: smooth motion that doesn't depend on frame rate, a character that tilts
  with its speed, a flap animation, parallax background layers, particles on flap
  and crash, a small screen shake on crash, and a short vibration on crash where the
  browser supports it.
- Difficulty: start forgiving, then slowly narrow the gaps and speed up as the score
  grows.
- Sound: flap, point and crash sounds, plus a mute toggle. Start audio only after the
  first tap.
- Polish: one consistent art style and color palette, a readable score at the top,
  nothing under the notch or the home bar.

When you're done, check that the game actually works and fix anything that's broken.
Then tell me in a few lines what you built and how to run it.

title: Little Agent Island: Cozy Interactive AI Agent World
author: kinderlayer
prompt:
Build me a single-file interactive HTML artifact: a cozy little world where my AI agents live and work, shown as cute characters.

Make one adorable character for each of my agents/bots, each with its own little house. If I give you a list of my agents and their jobs, use those; if not, create a small friendly team (a scout, a builder, a reviewer, a router, a helper) as placeholders I can rename. Characters are soft, round, big-eyed, each a different color.

Behaviour, animated and alive:
- By DAY the characters walk around and "work", with little speech bubbles showing what each is doing (e.g. "searching...", "building...", "checking...", "routing..."). They path softly, idle-bob, blink.
- A slow DAY to NIGHT cycle: at night the sky turns deep blue, stars come out, the characters walk home, their windows glow warm, a tiny "zzz" floats up. In the morning they wake and come back out.
- Click a character to open a small card: name, role, and what it's doing right now.

Style: cozy, charming, premium - warm watercolor or soft low-poly, your call. Aim for "this is adorable, I could watch it forever." Make it beautiful, use lots of tokens, iterate until you're genuinely proud. No external assets — draw everything in code (SVG/canvas/CSS). It should just run.

When a character finishes a task, a tiny sparkle or "+1" floats up. Keep it calm and cute, not busy.

title: Pirate Jelly Interactive WebGPU Diorama
author: vib3coded
prompt:
Create a self-contained interactive WebGPU/WGSL page "Pirate Jelly" — part of a "Material Studies" series of jelly dioramas. Single HTML file, no external models, textures, fonts or libraries; everything procedural. English UI.

LOOK & LAYOUT
- A square block of translucent jelly sea (≈5.2 × 5.2 units) standing on a paper-studio floor; the camera looks in at the front corner at ~27°. The block's cut faces show candy strata (chocolate bedrock, caramel clay, a shell band, vanilla sand); the sea surface and walls refract and tint what's behind them, with caustics on the sea floor, light shafts, a tinted caustic shadow on the floor, foam lace on the shoreline and a bright meniscus on the cut edges.
- A small tropical island toward the back: sandy beach, a cove facing the viewer, a mossy jungle hump with ~9 gummy palms (ringed caramel trunks, translucent fronds that flutter), lumpy gummy bushes with flowers, ferns, beach grass, rocks around the shore.
- SKULL ROCK at the island's west tip, standing in the shallows: a cartoon skull sculpted as a signed-distance field (cranium, cheekbones, jaws, deep eye sockets, heart-shaped nose, crack on the crown, rock strata and noise, moss on top, a wet band at the waterline), meshed with surface nets; two rows of separate box teeth set into a carved grin. At night its eye sockets glow like a candle-lit cave.
- A PIRATE SHIP riding at anchor in front of the island, seen at three-quarters from the stern: black hull with an ochre gunport strake, red bottom, gunports with cannons, raised quarterdeck with lit stern windows and a stern lantern, three masts (square courses and topsails on fore and main, a gaff sail on the mizzen, a jib to the bowsprit), shrouds and stays, and a Jolly Roger (skull and crossed bones drawn procedurally in the shader) streaming aft. Her anchor chain runs from the bow down through the jelly to an anchor lying on the sea floor.
- The camp on the cove beach: a campfire (stone ring, teepee of logs with glowing ends, embers, a tripod with a pot, two seating logs), an iron-bound treasure chest under a leaning palm with a hinged lid and a heap of gold and gems inside, a shovel in a sand heap, barrels, a crate, a pyramid of round shot, a rum bottle, a rowing boat pulled up with its bow on the sand, and an "X" scored in the sand.
- On the sea floor: the bow half of an old wreck lying on its side with ribs showing and its broken mast beside it, swaying kelp, a few doubloons, bubbles caught in the jelly.

SIMULATION
- Linear shallow-water waves on a staggered grid with a little surface tension (springy jelly); the block can be tipped and the sea sloshes and the jelly wobbles (shear + squash).
- The ship floats on 10 buoyancy points (heave, pitch, roll), is pushed by a gently veering offshore breeze, held by an elastic anchor rode at the bow, and weathervanes into the wind. Her displaced volume is handed back to the sea, so she makes a wake.
- Rigid bodies: cannonballs (dense, fly in a clean arc, punch a crater, sink and roll on the floor), barrels (float on their side), doubloons (flutter down and settle flat). All interact with the sea (buoyancy, drag, splashes, bubbles), the terrain, the skull, the props, the palm trunks and the ship's hull.
- One particle system: fire flames (additive), embers, woodsmoke, muzzle flash, white gunsmoke, sea spray, sand puffs, gold glints over the open chest, fireflies at night.

INTERACTION
- Tap the ship → fire the next gun on the side facing the viewer (ball, flash, smoke, recoil heel). Drag the ship → tow her against the rode; release → she drifts back to her anchor.
- Tap the chest → lid swings open/shut with a bounce; gold glitters. Tap the fire → it roars and throws sparks. Tap the X → three doubloons pop out of the sand.
- Drag across the water to make waves; drag a side of the block to tip it; pick up and throw balls/barrels/coins; drag a palm to bend it; drag empty space or right-drag to orbit; wheel/pinch to zoom.

TIME OF DAY
- A slider from Noon → Afternoon → Golden hour → Sunset → Dusk → Night → Midnight. The sun lowers and warms, the backdrop turns peach, then the moon takes over (dim blue), stars appear on the backdrop, the page UI switches to a dark theme, and the campfire becomes the main light: a flickering point light that warms the sand, palms, sails and gold, reflects in the water, and lights the smoke from below. Stern windows and lantern glow.

UI (editorial, like the series)
- Top-left masthead: eyebrow "MATERIAL STUDIES", big italic serif title "Pirate / Jelly.", a short line of copy.
- Status pill (WebGPU · Live / Paused / Unavailable).
- Right glass panel: "The cove" — buttons Fire a gun / Doubloons / Barrel, a liveliness meter, tally Shots · Afloat · Sunk; "Flavour" — Turquoise, Rum (amber), Kraken (violet) jelly palettes; sliders Firmness, Wave damping, Time of day; Reset / Pause / Reset view.
- Bottom-left "How to play" line plus small instructions. Space fires a gun.
- Mobile: the panel becomes a bottom sheet; touch orbit and pinch zoom.
- Fallback card when WebGPU (or an adapter) isn't available. Respect prefers-reduced-motion.

中微子：

直接穿过去。

重复几次。

最后画面越来越空。

只剩：

黑暗。

一个极其微弱的蓝点。

这时候不要使用复杂文字。

只让视觉告诉观众：

“它太难抓了。”

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
【九、南极冰层】
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

这是整支视频最重要的场景之一。

镜头从宇宙：

快速下降到地球。

南极出现。

镜头直接冲入冰层。

不要普通的地下剖面动画。

要做成真正电影级的：

Ice Dive。

冰层具有真实的：

折射
散射
晶体结构
裂隙
气泡
冰层纹理
体积光

镜头不断深入。

最终进入完全黑暗。

然后：

一个探测器亮起。

再一个。

再一个。

然后整个 IceCube 阵列在黑暗中逐渐显现。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
【十、IceCube 必须成为视觉符号】
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

IceCube 不要只画成“很多小球”。

必须设计成具有建筑感、神殿感、未来科技感的巨大三维探测器阵列。

数千个光学探测器形成：

巨大三维网格。

镜头可以：

穿过阵列
绕阵列
从下往上看
从顶部俯视
沿探测器之间高速飞行

冰层和探测器形成巨大的尺度反差：

宏大的冰层
+
微小的探测器
+
极其微弱的蓝光

产生高级感。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
【十一、最重要的科学 VFX】
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

中微子进入冰层。

镜头跟随。

突然进入：

Extreme Macro。

从冰层：

→ 分子
→ 原子
→ 原子核

中微子发生相互作用。

这里绝对不能做成普通爆炸。

必须展示：

中微子相互作用
→ 产生带电粒子
→ 带电粒子高速穿过冰
→ 产生 Cherenkov 光

最终形成：

巨大的蓝色光锥。

这是全片最重要的视觉高潮。

蓝色光锥在冰中传播。

照亮周围冰晶。

反射到探测器。

整个 IceCube 阵列开始亮起。

这一刻必须有：

“WOW”级别的视觉冲击。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
【十二、蓝光与探测器】
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

探测器不要同时亮。

必须：

一个
→ 一个
→ 两个
→ 五个
→ 十个
→ 数十个
→ 大量探测器

按照真实的空间关系依次响应。

每一个响应：

都有轻微蓝色光晕。

但不要使用廉价闪烁。

让它像：

“整个冰层突然活了起来”。

然后摄影机高速穿过这些探测器。

光线在空间中形成复杂但真实的轨迹。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
【十三、把复杂原理变成漂亮画面】
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

科学家并不是直接看见中微子。

他们看到的是：

光。

所以必须明确表现：

中微子本身不可直接看到。

真正被探测的是：

Cherenkov light。

多个探测器：

记录位置。

记录到达时间。

把这些点：

连接。

形成：

三维空间轨迹。

不要使用普通折线图。

应该形成一种：

“数据正在自己生长出来”的视觉效果。

粒子轨迹从数据点中逐渐生成。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
【十四、时间差定位】
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

这是必须讲清楚的核心科学原理。

不同探测器：

不是同时亮。

而是：

这个先亮。

那个后亮。

再一个亮。

再一个亮。

把这些时间信息可视化。

但不要做成 Excel。

可以使用：

微弱时间数字
光点
波前
空间轨迹
粒子路径

最终：

所有数据融合。

形成一个巨大的三维方向箭头。

箭头向上延伸。

穿过冰层。

穿过地球。

进入宇宙。

最终指向一个遥远的宇宙源。

画面完成：

SOURCE RECONSTRUCTION

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
【十五、最终宇宙尺度】
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

最后不要停留在 IceCube。

摄影机必须继续后退。

IceCube
→ 南极
→ 地球
→ 月球轨道
→ 太阳系
→ 银河系
→ 更大的宇宙

蓝色轨迹继续向远处延伸。

然后让观众突然意识到：

刚才那个几乎看不见的粒子，

来自极其遥远的宇宙。

最终形成：

一个微小蓝点
连接
整个宇宙。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
【十六、最终视觉高潮】
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

最终不是简单出现：

“THE END”。

而是做一个真正的电影级收束。

画面：

黑色宇宙。

一束蓝色中微子轨迹横穿画面。

轨迹逐渐形成三个不同的宇宙观测方式：

LIGHT
GRAVITATIONAL WAVES
NEUTRINOS

然后：

前两条逐渐淡去。

只留下：

NEUTRINOS

最后出现：

A NEW WINDOW TO THE UNIVERSE

随后全部熄灭。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
【十七、Motion Design】
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

必须使用高级 Motion Design 思维。

包括：

Particle System
Point Cloud
Volumetric Light
Light Trails
3D Camera
Depth of Field
Motion Blur
Procedural Animation
Particle Flow
Particle-to-Line
Line-to-Particle
Data-driven Animation
Physics-based Motion
Scale Transition
Camera Fly Through
Volumetric Compositing
Depth Compositing
Ray Tracing Look
Subtle Bloom
Film Grain

所有动画必须有：

重量
惯性
速度
加速度
缓冲
空间关系

禁止：

机械平移
机械缩放
PPT 式出现
模板化科技转场

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
【十八、SRT 驱动】
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

我会提供 SRT。

SRT 是唯一时间来源。

必须读取：

歌词开始时间
歌词结束时间
句子长度
停顿
重复
副歌
段落
情绪变化

然后自动决定：

镜头长度
镜头数量
镜头切换
Camera Movement
Visual Punch
高潮
留白

不要输出任何固定时间码。

不要预设“每句歌词一个镜头”。

一句歌词可以对应一个长镜头。

也可以一句歌词对应多个快速镜头。

副歌可以进行视觉重复，但必须逐次升级。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
【十九、视觉节奏】
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

主歌：

神秘
克制
探索

Pre-Chorus：

逐渐加速
增加粒子
增加镜头运动

副歌：

宏大
爆发
蓝光
大量探测器
空间尺度变化

科学原理：

镜头变得精准
微观
清晰

最终副歌：

宏大
宇宙尺度
情绪释放

最终：

极度安静
黑色
一条蓝色粒子轨迹
消失。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
【二十、Typography】
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

字幕必须像电影 Title Design。

不要大段字幕。

不要把歌词全部打在画面上。

只强调关键概念：

NEUTRINO
ICECUBE
2 KM
CHERENKOV LIGHT
TIME
POSITION
DIRECTION
SOURCE

现代无衬线字体。

细体 / Medium。

极少颜色。

白色 + 冰蓝。

大量负空间。

文字出现必须有 Motion Design。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
【二十一、科学准确性】
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

必须保持科学准确。

特别注意：

不要说中微子“没有质量”。

不要把中微子画成普通光子。

不要把 Cherenkov radiation 描述成中微子直接发光。

正确逻辑：

中微子与物质发生相互作用
→ 产生带电粒子
→ 带电粒子在冰中高速运动
→ 产生 Cherenkov light
→ 光学传感器记录这些光
→ 根据空间和时间信息重建事件
→ 推断中微子方向。

如果为了视觉简化，必须保持这个因果关系。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
【二十二、最终审美判断】
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

每设计一个镜头，都问：

这个镜头是否：

1. 推进故事？
2. 解释科学？
3. 具有电影感？
4. 有视觉记忆点？
5. 能和前后镜头自然连接？
6. 有真实空间尺度？
7. 有高级 Motion Design？
8. 不像普通 AI 科普？
9. 不像 PPT？
10. 不像科技模板？

如果只是“好看”，但不能推进故事：

删除。

如果只是“解释”，但画面不震撼：

重新设计。

最终必须达到：

“电影级科学视觉大片”

而不是：

“漂亮的 AI 科普视频”。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
【最终输出】
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

在读取我提供的 SRT 后，请输出：

1. 完整视觉叙事结构
2. 每段歌词对应的视觉概念
3. 每个镜头的具体画面
4. Camera Movement
5. 3D Scene
6. VFX
7. Particle Design
8. Lighting
9. Transition
10. Typography
11. Motion Design
12. AE 实现建议
13. Blender / Cinema 4D / Houdini 实现建议
14. 哪些镜头应该做成视觉高潮
15. 哪些镜头应该留白
16. 如何让整支片保持统一的视觉 DNA

重点：

不要为了增加镜头数量而增加镜头。

宁可一个镜头非常震撼、非常完整、非常电影化，也不要十个普通镜头。

最终目标：

让观众看完以后不仅觉得“很酷”，

而且能够用一句话解释这项诺贝尔物理学奖：

“科学家把探测器埋进南极冰里，等中微子偶尔撞上冰中的原子，产生蓝色 Cherenkov 光，再通过数千个探测器记录的时间和位置，反推出它来自宇宙的哪个方向。”

这才是这支动画成功的标准。

title: Polymarket Election Odds Explainer Video via HyperFrames
author: condzxyz
prompt:
Faça um vídeo de 30 s em 16:9 (1920×1080, 30 fps) no HyperFrames (npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes), com narração, no padrão de qualidade abaixo.

## PEDIDO
- Tema: o Polymarket dá 84% de chance ao Flávio Bolsonaro no 2º turno de 2026 (25/10).
- Foco positivo no Flávio, em quatro pontos:
  1. o mercado que acertou o Trump em 2024 aponta Flávio;
  2. as pesquisas do 1º turno davam Lula na frente, e deu Flávio;
  3. Flávio teve 5 milhões de votos a mais que o pai em 2022;
  4. quem proibiu o Polymarket no Brasil foi o governo Lula.
- CTA: compartilhar para mais gente ver os fatos.
- Onde vai postar: X e LinkedIn. Versão 9:16 só se eu pedir.

## FATOS (confirme na web no dia da postagem; as odds mudam)
- Polymarket, 06/10/2026, 14h de Nova York: Flávio 84,2% × Lula 15,5%, com US$ 174 milhões negociados (Rio Times).
- EUA 2024: na véspera, o Polymarket dava Trump 58,1% × Kamala Harris 41,9%, com as pesquisas nacionais em empate; Trump venceu (Fox Business e The Block, nov/2024). O adversário foi a Harris, NÃO o Biden.
- Véspera do 1º turno de 2026, votos válidos (Gazeta do Povo, 05/10/2026):
  - Datafolha: Lula 45 × 42
  - Quaest: 46 × 45
  - AtlasIntel: 47 × 44,1
  - PoderData: 45 × 43
  - CNT/MDA: 47,8 × 42,1
  - Só a Gerp dava Flávio na frente: 46 × 44.
- Resultado do 1º turno (TSE): Flávio 47,03% × Lula 45,16%.
  - Flávio teve 56.104.503 votos.
  - Jair Bolsonaro teve 51.072.345 no 1º turno de 2022, ou seja, cerca de 5 milhões a menos.
- Proibição:
  - a Res. CMN 5.298/2026 proíbe contratos sobre eventos eleitorais (em vigor desde 04/05/2026; CNN Brasil, 24/04/2026);
  - o Ministério da Fazenda mandou bloquear o Polymarket;
  - por isso a frase é "o governo Lula proibiu".

## REGRAS
- Odds de aposta não são pesquisa. Todo % do Polymarket vem com "Mercado de apostas · não é pesquisa" (risco de enquete sem registro: Lei 9.504, art. 33 §5º; Res. TSE 23.600).
- As pesquisas "erraram", nunca "falsas" (art. 323 do Código Eleitoral).
- Não escreva "comprovou que funciona"; escreva "acertou o Trump".
- Selo "Narração gerada por IA" visível o vídeo todo (Res. TSE 23.610, art. 9-B).
- Fotos reais só com licença livre (Wikimedia Commons, Agência Senado), com crédito no fim. Nunca gerar nem alterar rosto com IA.

## ROTEIRO (texto exato da voz)
[dramatically] O mercado que acertou o Trump dá oitenta e quatro por cento pro Flávio. [serious] No primeiro turno, cinco de seis institutos davam Lula na frente. [dramatically] Deu Flávio. Cinquenta e seis milhões de votos. Cinco milhões a mais que o pai em vinte e dois. [serious] E quem proibiu o Polymarket no Brasil? O governo Lula. Não é pesquisa. É dinheiro de verdade. [dramatically] Compartilhe. Mais gente precisa ver os fatos.

## VOZ (ElevenLabs pelo conector)
- Modelo eleven_v4, voz "Randel - Deep Epic" (jkiD8IhCU1i2V7VvmNwi).
- Gere 4 takes, transcreva com whisper (timestamp por palavra) e escolha o mais preciso.
- Números por extenso. Não use IPA entre barras: a v4 lê em voz alta.
- Pausas de respiro:
  - 0,5 s depois de "Trump";
  - 0,45 s antes de "Deu Flávio";
  - 0,2 s antes de "Cinquenta";
  - 0,55 s antes de "O governo Lula";
  - 0,15 s antes de "Não é pesquisa";
  - 0,5 s antes de "Compartilhe".
- A voz começa em 0,13 s e termina por volta de 26,2 s.

## CENAS (cada corte na palavra exata; cada elemento entra quando a palavra é dita)
0. Capa, 0–1 s. O quadro 0 é a thumbnail, sem fade.
   - Foto do Flávio sorrindo à direita.
   - À esquerda: "POLYMARKET · 06/10/2026", "84%" gigante em mono e "CHANCE DE FLÁVIO VENCER".
   - Título serif "O mercado que acertou o Trump."
   - Rodapé "Mercado de apostas · não é pesquisa eleitoral".
1. 1 s → "dá". Retrato oficial do Trump.
   - "EUA · ELEIÇÃO DE 2024", "58%", "Trump no Polymarket · pesquisas: empate".
   - Carimbo "Acertou." com marca-texto amarelo.
   - Fonte no rodapé.
2. "dá" → "No". Layout espelhado: outra foto do Flávio à esquerda, texto à direita.
   - Contador 0→84% começando em "oitenta".
   - Barra azul até 84,2% e selo "Mercado de apostas · não é pesquisa".
3. "No" → "Deu". Urna escurecida ao fundo.
   - Folha de papel levemente inclinada: "O que diziam as pesquisas · véspera do 1º turno · votos válidos".
   - A partir de "cinco", as 5 linhas entram em cascata com a etiqueta vermelha "Lula na frente".
   - Em "Lula", entra a linha da Gerp, destacada em azul: "Flávio na frente".
   - Fonte: Gazeta do Povo, 05/10/2026.
4. "Deu" → "Cinquenta". Flávio cercado de microfones.
   - "Deu Flávio." gigante (serif 800), com marca-texto em "Flávio."
   - Tarja "RESULTADO TSE · FLÁVIO 47,03% × LULA 45,16%".
5. "Cinquenta" → "E quem". Flávio no plenário.
   - Contador até 56.104.503.
   - Em "Cinco": barras de Jair 2022 (51.072.345, cinza) × Flávio 2026 (56.104.503, azul).
   - Em "pai": chip amarelo "+5 milhões de votos".
6. "E quem" → "Não". Palácio do Planalto escurecido.
   - Pergunta em duas linhas: "E quem proibiu o Polymarket / no Brasil?"
   - Em "Brasil?": documento no rodapé (Res. CMN 5.298/2026 e a ordem da Fazenda de bloquear).
   - Em "O governo": entra "O governo Lula." gigante, com marca-texto.
7. "Não" → "Compartilhe". Foto da bolsa.
   - "Não é pesquisa."
   - Em "É": "É dinheiro de verdade.", com marca-texto.
   - Chip "US$ 174 milhões negociados (Polymarket, 06/10)".
8. "Compartilhe" → 30 s. Rua lotada na região da 25 de Março, escurecida.
   - Ícone de compartilhar com "Compartilhe." gigante e "Mais gente precisa ver os fatos."
   - No hit final da música: "25 DE OUTUBRO · 2º TURNO".
   - Fontes e créditos em faixa escura no rodapé.

title: Gouo Canvas UI Product Promo Video
author: xgouoo
prompt:
# 任务：为「光构 Gouo Canvas」制作产品宣传视频

## 背景
光构是我做的 AI 图片创作平台（GitHub：zhs1234/gouo-canvas），有三个工作区：生成图片、无限画布、创作 Agent。请先 clone 仓库，阅读首页源码 src/components/landing/（LandingPage.tsx、landing.css）和用户指南 docs/zh-CN/user-guide.md，再开始制作。

## 规格
- 16:9，1920×1080，30fps，约 60 秒，MP4（H.264）
- 无配音、无背景音乐，只有轻柔的交互音效

## 素材（重要）
- 片中所有出图只用首页的真实生成图：public/landing/preview-{1..3}-{1..4}.webp
  - 第 1 组 牛排：「黑金质感的牛排商品图，雪花纹理特写，高级餐厅风格」
  - 第 2 组 刺绣花鸟：「立体刺绣风格的花鸟插画，米白底色，柔和配色」
  - 第 3 组 雨夜街角：「雨后的城市街角，霓虹倒影，电影感」
- 片中打出的提示词必须是这些图的真实提示词，不能编造
- 不使用 public/inspiration 里的灵感库图片（第三方示例图，商用许可未核实）
- 不使用 docs 里的截图作品（文档手绘示意图）
- 没有真实素材的效果不伪造（例如局部重绘只演示涂抹操作，不展示修改后结果）
- 画面角落加小字：「界面为演示动画 · 图片均为光构真实生成」

## 视觉风格（沿用首页动效）
- 开场与收尾：首页暖色流体彩雾（7 团模糊色块缓慢漂移）+ 颗粒噪点；白色大字逐行从遮罩中升起；作品卡片白边、倾斜、轻微浮动
- 功能段：用 HTML 重建光构深色产品界面（侧栏、余额、输入框、画布、Agent 对话），不直接贴截图
- 配色：纸色 #faf8f3、墨色 #171719、强调色 #c26855；缓动 cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)
- 出图动效沿用首页的「显影」：从模糊、低饱和逐张变清晰
- 左下角玻璃质感字幕卡：编号 + 功能名 + 一句标题 + 一句说明

## 模拟鼠标
全程由一个模拟鼠标操作：平滑移动、点击时缩小并出现涟漪、悬停反馈、按住拖拽。鼠标位置要实时对准目标元素，不写死坐标。

## 分镜
1. 开场（0–6s）：首页首屏，「把灵感 / 构造成图像」升起，鼠标点「开始创作」进入产品
2. 生成图片（6–27s）
   - 点输入框，逐字打出牛排提示词；点「自定义参数」选 4 张，预计扣费同步变为 80 积分
   - 点发送，4 张牛排依次显影，提示「生成完成，已保存到作品库」
   - 悬停一张，点 ♥ 收藏（出现提示条），点「编辑输出」，缩略图飞入参考图位
   - 打开遮罩编辑器，蓝色画笔涂抹背景，保存后输入「把遮罩区域换成白色大理石台面」
3. 无限画布（27–41s）
   - 切换到画布；工具栏添加文本节点「米白底色，柔和配色」，再添加生成配置节点「立体刺绣风格的花鸟插画」
   - 从文本节点拖线连到配置节点（显示「已连接 1 段文本」），张数改为 2，点生成
   - 两张刺绣花鸟作为结果节点从右侧连出并显影
   - 镜头拉远，旁边是「作品库 · 牛排商品图」分组，小地图亮起
4. 创作 Agent（41–55s）
   - 点「Agent」进入对话，输入「想要一张雨后城市夜景，霓虹倒影，有电影感」
   - Agent 流式回复，说明已整理出提示词「雨后的城市街角，霓虹倒影，电影感」
   - 依次出现工具卡：读取画布 → 生成图片（已提交 → 已生成 2 张，显影雨夜街角）→ 修改画布
   - 切回画布，「Agent · 雨夜街角」分组出现，提示「Agent 已在画布中添加 2 个节点」
5. 收尾（55–63s）：浅色彩雾 + 点阵，「从一句话 / 开始。」，三个功能标签、logo、「开始创作」按钮（鼠标点击）
全片余额随每次生成递减，与预计扣费一致。

## 音效（要优雅、轻柔、克制）
- 无背景音乐、无铺底和弦
- 点击：低频、缓起、重低通，几乎只剩一点触感
- 打字：极轻的触感声
- 图片显影：慢起的柔和单音，同一调性（C 大调），不要清脆或「叮」的感觉
- 生成完成：一声很轻的浮现音，不用双音提示
- 转场：柔和气息声，不用噪声风声
- 收尾：一个舒展的和弦，音量也要克制
- 整体音量偏低（峰值约 -15 dBFS），所有声音与画面动作精确对齐
- 音效全部用程序合成，不使用外部素材

## 技术实现
- 单个 HTML 页面 + 确定性时间轴：render(t) 只根据时间 t 计算每个元素的状态
- Playwright 逐帧截图，ffmpeg 编码，可分段并行渲染后拼接
- 音效用 Python（numpy/scipy）合成为 wav，再与视频合并
- 先渲染关键帧截图检查对位，再出全片

title: Seamless Morphing UI Motion Design
author: finnardley
prompt:
<inputs>
Ask me for: 4 photos (a mountain valley at sunrise, a top-down drone shot of a roundabout, a latte being poured from above, the sun over the sea at golden hour), one accent color (mine is violet #A898FF), and a royalty-free song around 118 BPM with a drop (e.g. Pixabay, free for commercial use).
</inputs>

<direction>
Apple-level motion. One object, never cut: every state is born out of the one before it, a knob opens like a lens into a photo, a card shrinks into the sun, a row in a list grows into a full photo. Night #0A0A0C to day #F2F0EB and back, ink #0E0E10 UI, real photos for the big moments, frosted liquid glass for small panels, one clean font (Geist, Geist Mono for times). Every morph uses one curve, cubic-bezier(.45,0,.15,1), springs only for pop-ins. Text rises through a mask, never fades. The camera zooms so each state fills about 60% of the frame and creeps in through every hold. The last frame is the first frame, so it loops.
Banned: crossfades, cuts, grey mush between colors, clip-art icons, glows, bouncy easing, dead time, anything that looks like a template.
</direction>

<structure>
118 BPM, 47 beats, the drop lands on the first release.
6:30 alarm pill → slide to stop, the sunrise shows through behind the knob → release on the drop, the knob irises into the sunrise card → a glass droplet rises into a weather panel, 14° counts to 18° → the card shrinks into the sun → the sun floods the screen into day → its core becomes a violet location dot → an aerial map unfolds around it → the route draws, the dot drives, "8 min" counts to "Arrived", it bounces on the pin → the pin irises into a latte photo → "Pay $4.20" grows out of the card → tap → loader → check → the card folds into the check → the check stretches into a Focus toggle → it opens into today's schedule, a line sweeps 9:00 to 18:00 → the 18:00 row grows into a sunset → the card closes on the sun, the sun turns into the moon → night floods back → the moon becomes the 6:30 pill.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML canvas, square 1440x1440. Every frame is computed from time inside seek(t): no CSS transitions, no timers, no state carried between frames.
2. One shape grammar: pill 640x120 → card 620x780 radius 64 → circle 240 → map 760 square → portrait 560x780 → check 96 → pill 560x130 → schedule 620x520 → card 620x780 → moon 200 → pill 300x96.
3. Reveals are circular clips: the photo is drawn at its final position inside a circle that grows from the exact point it is born from. Floods grow by the square root of progress so the area changes evenly.
4. Liquid glass: blur a copy of the frame under the panel, magnify its inner edge 1.08x, add a white tint, a top highlight and a 2px white rim.
5. Camera zoom per state: 2.3 alarm, 1.2 cards, 2.5 sun and moon, 1.18 map, 2.1 check, 1.7 toggle, 1.35 schedule, gliding on the same curve.
6. Analyze the song with numpy for the beat grid and land the drop on the release. Every event gets its own real sound, placed by its measured peak.
7. Render with Playwright: 8 subframes per frame, blended for motion blur at 60fps. Render a sheet of stills first and fix anything cramped or cheap looking.
</build>

<gotchas>
A photo that irises open must already sit where it will end up, or it slides when the clip finishes. Text inside a growing card needs its own timing or it vanishes before anyone reads it. Never let the card underneath peek out around a growing photo. Make the last frame identical to the first or the loop stutters.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for the inputs, then show me the state list on the beat grid before you write any code.
</start>

title: Fictional Fashion Commercial Direction with Claude Opus 5.5 and MiniMax H3
author: ito1217yo
prompt:
